solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pottery that is new in appearance

indicators.note: 'in' places the first pair of pieces inside the final word of the clue

blocks.note: i.e. is the Latin abbreviation for 'that is'
N is the standard abbreviation for new
one's face is one's appearance or look

explanation.surface: A potter's work looks brand new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' splits the last word in two, with the other pieces dropped into the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: Faience is a kind of glazed earthenware, a type of pottery.

clue.text: Flank is replacing one for groin

indicators.note: one thing replacing another takes its place in the word

blocks.note: an means one, the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An anatomy note: the side of the body stands in for the groin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'groin' is not anatomy but the old verb to grumble or fret, which is what Scots flisk means.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers glosses the old verb groin as to grumble, and the Scots flisk as to fret or be restless.

clue.text: Where some believe the world began, half of it seen in creation of archangel

definitions.text: Where some believe the world began

indicators.note: half of a two-letter word is a single letter, here the front one
a creation is something made anew, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A creation myth in which an archangel helped shape the world.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Genesis; the answer is the Australian Aboriginal Dreamtime.
explanation.definitionFit: Alcheringa is the Dreamtime of Aboriginal belief, the mythic era when the world was formed.

clue.text: Having some notion I act accepting answer

indicators.note: a word accepting another takes it inside itself

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: Someone with a vague idea acts on it and takes an answer.
explanation.walkthrough: Ideaed is a rare word, also spelt idea'd; the clue reads naturally as 'I act'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideaed means furnished with ideas, so having some notion.

clue.text: Vintage pud that could provide stuffing for beanfeast

indicators.note: the stuffing is what fills the inside, so the outer letters of the word are discarded
'could provide' says the answer can be rearranged to yield the letters described

blocks.note: taken as written; the filling runs between the B and the final AST

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned pudding stuffed into a feast.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: rearrange the answer to get the filling of B...AST. Pud is not pudding but a paw or hand; 'Vintage' marks the word obsolete.
explanation.definitionFit: Neafe is an obsolete word for a fist, and pud is a child's word for a hand or paw.

clue.text: Carriage support has enough power to drag behind

blocks.note: to trail is to drag behind

explanation.surface: A horse-drawn carriage strong enough to pull a load behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantrail is a timber running along a railway carriage beneath the roof, supporting it.

clue.text: Drunk in confusion, grabbing attention

indicators.note: a word grabbing another clutches it inside

blocks.note: pied type is jumbled type, in printers' confusion
to give an eye to something is to pay attention

explanation.surface: A drunk, muddled, clutches at someone's attention.
explanation.walkthrough: Printers call jumbled type pie, so pied means thrown into confusion.
explanation.definitionFit: Pie-eyed is slang for very drunk.

clue.text: Poet's company, sad excluded from romantic enterprising

indicators.note: something excluded from a larger whole is taken out of it, leaving the rest

blocks.note: a crusade is a romantic, idealistic enterprise

explanation.surface: A melancholy poet's companions drop out of some dreamy venture.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove SAD from CRUSADE to leave CRUE, Spenser's spelling of 'crew'; 'Poet's' marks the word as poetic or archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: CRUE is an old poetic spelling of crew, a band or group of people, hence a company.

clue.text: Head of cuisine, male preferred to female?

definitions.text: Head of cuisine, male preferred to female?

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
placed before, as a preference ranks one ahead of another

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A wry question whether kitchens choose men over women as their bosses.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: the head of a kitchen, often a man preferred over a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A chef is literally the head cook of a kitchen; the question mark nods at the male-dominated trade.

clue.text: I learn, mostly active after changing teaching aids

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
changing letters means shifting them into a new order

blocks.note: A is the grammatical abbreviation for active

explanation.surface: A student says they learn better through hands-on activity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places A behind I LEAR before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Realia are real objects used in a classroom to illustrate lessons, a kind of teaching aid.

clue.text: Examiners led astray about leaving out less PT

indicators.note: letters led astray wander off their proper course into a new order
less means minus, so the two named letters are subtracted
about means around, so the jumbled letters surround the rest

explanation.surface: Examiners have been misled about skipping physical training.
explanation.walkthrough: PT looks like physical training; it is just two letters taken from EXCEPT.
explanation.definitionFit: Edexcel is a British exam board, a body that sets and marks school examinations.

clue.text: Daughter to bring up, I face gloom as of old

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
to rear a child is to bring it up
to head something is to face or confront it

explanation.surface: A parent raising a daughter dreads the gloom ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as of old' belongs to the definition, flagging an archaic word (Spenser's).
explanation.definitionFit: Drearihead is an obsolete word for dreariness, a state of melancholy gloom.

clue.text: Performance on rink? I give up if old and cold inside (8, two words)

indicators.note: something inside another word sits within it, splitting it

blocks.note: to cede is to give up or surrender
an is an archaic word for 'if'
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A skater about to quit as they grow old and cold.
explanation.walkthrough: An for 'if' is archaic, as in Shakespeare's 'an it please you'; 'old' flags that.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice dance is a routine performed by skating partners on an ice rink.

clue.text: What'll alter males' moods regarding membranous patches?

indicators.note: something that alters the letters changes them into a different order

explanation.surface: A question about what changes men's tempers.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites hormones as the answer; the letters of the two words are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A desmosome is a small patch of thickened cell membrane that binds adjacent cells, so desmosomal relates to such patches.

clue.text: Fish obtained on ship's bow

indicators.note: a ship's bow is its front end, so only the first letter of the word is wanted

explanation.surface: A fish landed on the front deck of a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' means placed after: HAD sits on S.
explanation.definitionFit: The shad is a herring-like fish that swims upriver to spawn.

clue.text: Expression from arbitrator and what he administers?

blocks.note: lex is Latin for law, which a referee applies

explanation.surface: A remark coming from a referee, and the rules he enforces.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that LEX for what a referee applies is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers gives reflex as a reflected image or an outward manifestation, hence an expression of something.

clue.text: Mouse producing squeak between King and Queen?

blocks.note: K is King in chess notation
eek is a squeak of fright
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A rodent squeaking between royals, as in a nursery rhyme.
explanation.walkthrough: Mouse is not the rodent but slang for a black eye, which Scots call a keeker.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mouse and keeker are slang for a black eye, a bruise round the socket.

clue.text: Typical of early bishop, mounting funeral with Gaelic John

indicators.note: in a down answer, mounting means climbing upwards, so the word is read bottom to top

blocks.note: a tangi is a Maori funeral ceremony
Ian is the Scottish Gaelic form of John

explanation.surface: An ancient bishop's funeral cortege climbing a hill with a Highlander called John.
explanation.walkthrough: TANGI read upwards is IGNAT. The early bishop is St Ignatius of Antioch.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignatian means relating to Ignatius, a first-century bishop of Antioch.

clue.text: Purse firm becomes cast if this

blocks.note: firm is FAST; one letter must turn into another for it to become CAST, and 'this' is that condition read as a statement

explanation.surface: A company's money changes hands, as cast-off funds.
explanation.walkthrough: FAST (firm) becomes CAST if F is C: write that condition as one word, FISC.
explanation.definitionFit: The fisc is the public treasury, the state's purse.

clue.text: To affirm on oath thus, we finesse within (7, two words)

indicators.note: within places the preceding words inside the other piece

explanation.surface: Swearing an oath with a certain delicacy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thus' supplies the outer pair of letters and the other two words go inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To swear to something is to affirm it on oath as true.

clue.text: Manage plays with set? One featuring in dramatis personae (9, two words)

indicators.note: to play with something is to fiddle with it, moving its parts around

explanation.surface: A theatre manager works with scenery for a production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plays' and 'set' look theatrical, which is the disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: The dramatis personae is a cast list, and actors often appear in it under a professional alias.

clue.text: Loudspeaker to waver with being installed

indicators.note: a thing installed is fitted inside something else

blocks.note: to teeter is to waver unsteadily
W is the abbreviation for with

explanation.surface: A speaker that wobbles once it is fitted.
explanation.walkthrough: W goes into TEETER after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweeter is a small loudspeaker unit that reproduces high-frequency sound.

clue.text: Types of convolvulus afflicted by gusts?

blocks.note: to be with a cold is to be afflicted by it

explanation.surface: Climbing plants battered by the wind.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the whimsical split of the plant name.
explanation.definitionFit: Withwind is an old name for bindweed, a convolvulus that twines round other plants.

clue.text: One among 10,000, without exception (6, three words)

indicators.note: something among others is placed in their midst

blocks.note: a toman is a Persian term for 10,000, also a coin of that many dinars

explanation.surface: Someone who is one in ten thousand, with no exceptions.
explanation.walkthrough: Toman is a Persian word for ten thousand, and later a coin.
explanation.definitionFit: To a man is an idiom meaning every single one, with no exception.

clue.text: Flowering plant: chance upon one when sun's in

indicators.note: a letter that is in a word sits inside it

blocks.note: to come upon by chance; come alone here means happen upon
S is the abbreviation for sun

explanation.surface: A gardener stumbles upon a single bloom on a sunny day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when sun's in' means with the sun's letter placed inside the first piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmea is another name for cosmos, a garden plant with daisy-like flowers.

clue.text: Scotch immediately? Single knocked back with a dash of water

indicators.note: a drink knocked back goes down in one, and the word is read in the backward direction
a dash is a tiny splash, so only the first letter of the following word is used

explanation.surface: Whisky to be drunk at once, a single downed with a splash of water.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotch is the language label, not the drink; Scots enow means presently.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots usage enow means just now or presently, so immediately is a fair equivalent.

clue.text: The plash of oars I love, easy on the ears

indicators.note: a plash is a splash, which throws everything into disorder

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A rower delights in the pleasant splash of the oars.
explanation.walkthrough: Easy on the ears is the definition: arioso is melodious.
explanation.definitionFit: Arioso describes a melodious, songlike style, pleasant for the listener.

clue.text: Registers in desks, top removed

indicators.note: with the top taken off, that part of the word is dropped

blocks.note: rolltops are desks with a sliding slatted lid

explanation.surface: Records kept in desks with their lids taken off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top' is not the first letter but the word TOP itself, cut from inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Rolls are official lists or registers, as in an electoral roll.

clue.text: This orange is inedible, round and green

explanation.surface: A fruit that is round and green cannot be eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This orange' points to the osage orange, whose large green fruit is inedible.
explanation.definitionFit: The Osage orange is a North American tree whose wrinkled green fruit is not edible.

clue.text: Love feasts dad's back occupying a long time

indicators.note: back means turned round, so the word is read right to left
one thing occupying another sits inside it

blocks.note: pa is a familiar name for dad

explanation.surface: Father has been away for a long while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dad's' is read as 'dad is', so dad is the subject that goes back and occupies.
explanation.definitionFit: Agapes were the communal meals of the early Church, held as feasts of brotherly love.

clue.text: Day in action requiring protective gear

indicators.note: a letter in a word sits inside it

blocks.note: a pas is a step, as in dancing
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: A day of fighting calls for protective kit.
explanation.walkthrough: D goes inside PA...S.
explanation.definitionFit: Pads are padded guards worn to protect the legs, as by cricketers.

clue.text: Crosses road finally before call for help

indicators.note: finally points to the end of the word, so just the last letter is kept

explanation.surface: Someone stranded at a road's end crosses and calls for help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crosses' looks like a verb; it is the plural noun for medals. 'before' puts D first.
explanation.definitionFit: The DSO, Distinguished Service Order, is a British military decoration in the form of a cross.

clue.text: I'm alert, puzzled about bit of magic – it offers three possible solutions

indicators.note: puzzled letters are confused, so they come out muddled
a bit is a small piece, here just the opening letter
about means around, so the muddled letters surround the small piece

explanation.surface: A conjuror stays alert and baffled over a magic trick.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole final clause, a description rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A trilemma is a choice between three alternatives, like a dilemma with an extra option.

clue.text: Bust of Shakespeare fan altered mistakenly

indicators.note: something altered by mistake has been changed into a different order

explanation.surface: A fan's bust of the playwright has been wrongly changed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bust of Shakespeare' looks like a statue; bust means bankrupt, in Shakespeare's word. 'altered' does double duty as fodder and part of the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's tradefalne means having fallen out of trade, that is bankrupt or bust.

clue.text: Recognizes what's broadcast, start to finish

indicators.note: the opening letter is carried round to the end of the word

explanation.surface: Someone acknowledges what's been on air from beginning to end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' suggests radio; it is scattering seed.
explanation.definitionFit: To own a fault is to acknowledge or admit it, so owns means recognizes.

clue.text: To prepare e.g. fish in kitchen, see e.g. Sam as cutting back here and there

definitions.text: To prepare e.g. fish in kitchen

indicators.note: back means turned round, so the little word is read in the opposite direction
letters cutting a word slice into it
here and there says the slicing happens at two separate points, one letter each

blocks.note: Uncle Sam personifies the USA, the example the clue points to

explanation.surface: A cookery instruction pointing the reader to a cross-reference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'here and there' says the two letters of the reversed word go in at different places: UN-S-C-A-LE.
explanation.definitionFit: To unscale a fish is to strip off its scales, a step in preparing it for cooking.
